Plot a self-organising map

Source: R/plot_functions.R
eemsom_plot_map.Rd

Different properties of the units are shown on the map.

Usage

eemsom_plot_map(
  som,
  type = "counts",
  colour = NULL,
  labels = FALSE,
  unit_labels = FALSE
)

Arguments

som

object of class eemsom, see eemsom

type

property to be shown:

  • "counts": number of samples mapped to each unit

  • "umatrix": unified distance matrix, mean Euclidean distance between the prototype of a unit and the prototypes of its direct neighbours. High values separate groups of similar units.

  • "quality": mean distance between the samples of a unit and its prototype, see eemsom_samples

  • "cluster": clusters of the units

  • "samples": samples as points on their units, the units are coloured by cluster if available

colour

optional vector with one value per sample (e.g. sampling site from metadata) used to colour the samples with type = "samples"

labels

logical, whether sample names are shown with type = "samples"

unit_labels

logical, whether the numbers of the units are shown. They are used by ggeem.eemsom, eemsom_codes and eemsom_samples.

Value

a ggplot object

Details

Neighbours are defined like in unit.distances: six units on hexagonal maps, eight units including the diagonals on rectangular maps.

With type = "samples", samples of the same unit are arranged in a circle around the centre of the unit.

Ejarque-Gonzalez and Butturini (2014) used the U-matrix to find regions of similar units and projected the samples, coloured by sampling site and hydrological conditions, onto the map to explore the patterns among samples.

References

Ejarque-Gonzalez, E., Butturini, A. (2014). Self-Organising Maps and Correlation Analysis as a Tool to Explore Patterns in Excitation-Emission Matrix Data Sets and to Discriminate Dissolved Organic Matter Fluorescence Components. PLoS ONE 9(6), e99618. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099618

See also

Other plots: eemsom_plot_cplane(), eemsom_plot_silhouette(), eemsom_plot_stability(), eemsom_plot_training(), ggeem.eemsom(), ggeem.eemsom_regions()

Examples

data(eem_list)

som <- eemsom(eem_list, rlen = 100, seed = 42)
eemsom_plot_map(som, unit_labels = TRUE)

eemsom_plot_map(som, type = "umatrix")

eemsom_plot_map(som, type = "samples", colour = substr(eem_names(eem_list), 1, 2), labels = TRUE)
